sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Rennes is tightening access to the centre in steps. A low-emission zone has applied inside the ring road since 1 January 2025, and the city page, updated on 20 March 2026, sets out planned stages: Crit'Air 5 and unclassified vehicles from 1 January 2027, Crit'Air 4 from 2029 and Crit'Air 3 from 2030, with park-and-ride sites still usable [0]. The historic centre is a limited-traffic zone with a speed cap of 20 km/h; the city lists five car parks with 2,200 spaces as open to everyone, though the list still names Vilaine, which closed in September 2025 [1]. Citing the urban-mobility dashboard, a local magazine reports that cars made up 47.2% of trips across the metropolis in 2023 and 31% inside the ring road [17].

Paid on-street parking has been widened and re-priced. Two extensions took place in 2025, from 16 June and 13 October, and a further one is announced from 16 November 2026 to parts of the Thabor, Saint-Hélier, Alphonse-Guérin and Saint-Martin districts, which the city describes as heavily saturated [3][6]. A city release of 1 July 2026 announced a tariff change of about 2% from 15 July 2026, with the post-parking charge rising from 40.60 to 41.60 euros in the red zone and from 25.40 to 26.20 euros in the green zone [2]. As of 13 October 2026 the city page gives those charges, a 4-hour maximum stay in the red zone and 8 hours in the green zone, and resident monthly passes at 49 euros (red) and 14.70 euros (green) [4]. In December 2025 a local magazine reported that the city would introduce a visitor pass at 3.20 euros a day for residents of paid sectors, up to 52 uses per household per year [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The biggest change in the centre is the loss of the Vilaine car park. C-Park announced on 31 July 2025 that it would close permanently on 1 September 2025 because of the scheme to reopen the covered river [10]. Demolition of the slab began on 13 October 2025, and by early April 2026 half of the 270 metres was gone, with completion expected by early June; the article gives no figure for spaces lost and names no replacement [11]. The next phase of the 29 million euro scheme for the quays and place de la République was due to start on 6 July 2026, with works to lay out public spaces from autumn 2026 to the end of 2028 [12].

The operator is also investing in its other garages. C-Park announced in October 2025 that 308 new interoperable charge points would be installed gradually, the first due in service in January 2026 [13], and the city page of 13 October 2026 still describes the 308 chargers as due in summer 2026 in nine car parks, at 1 euro to connect plus 0.40 euro per kWh plus the parking fee, without saying whether the rollout is finished [14]. In March 2025 resident subscriptions became available at the Hôtel Dieu car park, with 305 spaces on three levels, from 183 euros [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
As of 13 October 2026 the city lists twelve public C-Park car parks run by Citédia, plus eight park-and-ride sites that are free with a Star transit ticket; the page gives no capacities [8]. Rennes Métropole re-awarded the Star transit network to Keolis for seven years from the start of 2026 [9]. Since January 2024 on-street parking control has run on automatic number-plate reading vehicles and 14 handheld devices supplied by Egis to the public company Citédia Métropole under a five-year contract [7]. A data.gouv.fr dataset, last updated in 2016, describes an open API for the ten structured car parks; we did not check whether it still works [16].

Our data cover 15 car parks with 8,065 spaces from the metropolis's live feed, ten garages in the centre and five park-and-ride sites, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 47% on weekdays and 32% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The busiest garage is Chézy-Dinan (395 spaces), which averaged 74% and reached 92%, one of the five that the city lists as open to all [1]. Gare-Sud (990) averaged 64% on weekdays and 25% at weekends, reached 97% on a Wednesday at about 15:00 and was full for about 16% of the hours. Lices averaged 56%. At the other end the Kennedy garage (193 spaces) averaged 10% and Hôtel Dieu (285 in the feed against the 305 the operator states [15]) 16%. The park-and-ride sites fill on weekdays: Villejean-Université (356) and La Poterie (640) reached 100% and were full for 26% and 18% of the hours, and Henri Fréville (384) for 23%, while at weekends their occupancy falls by roughly a third to a half. These are two weeks of data.
